name: Willis Wall

waypoints.name: White River Campground
waypoints.directions: This route begins at White River Campground on the mountain's north side, at about 4,400 feet, now the practical way to reach Willis Wall. The traditional approach up the Carbon River Road is no longer usable: SR-165's Fairfax Bridge, the only public access to Carbon River, was permanently closed by the state highway department in April 2025 with no detour, turning that side into a roughly 19-mile one-way wilderness approach instead of a drive-in.

approach: Traditionally approached via the Carbon River Road to Ipsut Creek and the Carbon Glacier — but SR-165's Fairfax Bridge (the only public access to Carbon River) was permanently closed by WSDOT in April 2025 with no detour, making this a ~19-mile one-way wilderness approach via the Wonderland Trail. That way in is closed too while Mount Rainier National Park's fire closure stands: effective September 5, 2026 and until further notice, it closes the Wonderland Trail from the Carbon River Suspension Bridge to Frozen Lake near Sunrise, including Dick Creek camp, and the Moraine Park area. Many recent parties instead approach via White River/Glacier Basin, crossing the Winthrop Glacier over Curtis Ridge to reach the base of the wall.
